paper_metadata.title: Longitudinal Changes in Resting State Connectivity and White Matter Integrity in Adolescents With Sports-Related Concussion

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population and inclusion criteria. However, the sample size is small (n=16 SRC, n=12 controls), and the recruitment is limited to a single sports medicine department, which may introduce selection bias. The lack of information on the total number of eligible athletes vs. those who participated makes it difficult to assess the participation rate.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Thirty adolescent male football players (ages 14-18 years) were recruited from the Sports Medicine Department at Children's Healthcare of Atlanta to participate in this study.
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined by age, sex, sport, and clinical setting.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Participants included 16 adolescents who had sustained a SRC and 14 adolescent controls who had never sustained a SRC. Each control participant was age-matched and from the same football team as the participant with SRC.
items.reasoning: While the recruitment source is mentioned, the specific sampling frame (e.g., consecutive vs. convenience) is not explicitly stated.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (SRC) was defined by clinical assessment and GCS scores. The timing of the 'acute' measurement was strictly controlled (<7 days), and standardized protocols were used for all participants.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: concussion diagnosis as determined by a sideline assessment by the athletic trainer... GCS score of 13-15 as well as having less than 5 min of loss of consciousness.
items.reasoning: The definition of SRC is clinically specific and includes severity markers.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: imaging at time 1 was conducted within 7 days of the concussion and the participants endorsed at least two concussive symptoms
items.reasoning: The use of both clinical diagnosis and symptom verification at the time of scan increases reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.

items.reasoning: Standard clinical cut-points for mild TBI were used.

items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Both the control group and SRC group were imaged twice, 21 days apart (time 2) with the same imaging parameters.
items.reasoning: Standardized imaging and clinical protocols were applied across groups.

items.label: Method used for missing data

items.evidence_snippet: One participant with SRC did not return to the time 2 imaging scan and so was excluded from the analyses
items.reasoning: Listwise exclusion was used rather than imputation, which is acceptable for this sample size and low attrition.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using objective, automated neuroimaging (rs-fMRI, DTI) and a validated neurocognitive battery (ImPACT). The same parameters were used for all subjects, and the data-driven analysis (GICA) reduces assessor bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: investigate alterations in functional connectivity, white matter integrity, and cognitive abilities... at the acute phase (<7 days post-SRC) and at 21 days later
items.reasoning: Outcomes and follow-up intervals are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: rs-fMRI images were acquired using a single-shot T2*-weighted gradient-echo EPI pulse sequence... ImPACT neurocognitive battery (Lovell, 2015).
items.reasoning: The study uses established neuroimaging sequences and a widely validated clinical tool (ImPACT).

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Both the control group and SRC group were imaged twice, 21 days apart (time 2) with the same imaging parameters.
items.reasoning: Consistency in measurement setting and parameters is confirmed.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study matched controls by age and team, and excluded common comorbidities (ADHD, depression). However, the small sample size limited the ability to perform multivariable adjustment for other potential confounders like prior concussion history (which was present in 3 SRC participants but 0 controls).

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).

items.reasoning: The analysis relied on t-tests and correlations rather than multivariable models (e.g., ANCOVA) to adjust for variables like IQ or prior concussions.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used sophisticated, data-driven statistical methods (GICA, ICASSO, TOPUP) and corrected for multiple comparisons using FDR. The reporting is transparent regarding both significant and non-significant findings.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: GICA was conducted in three main steps... Stability analysis was conducted using ICASSO... corrected for multiple comparisons using a false discovery rate (FDR) cluster correction of p < .05.
items.reasoning: The analytical pipeline for both fMRI and DTI is described in high detail.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: The advantage to our approach for analyzing rs-fMRI using GICA and group connectometry for DTI is both are data-driven approaches without the need for selecting a priori ROIs.
items.reasoning: The use of data-driven approaches is justified as a way to avoid ROI bias.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: A series of two-sample t tests were conducted... Paired t tests were conducted to compare the SRC group at time 1... to time 2.
items.reasoning: The use of paired and independent t-tests is appropriate for the longitudinal, two-group design.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: No differences between the SRC group and control group were seen at follow-up imaging.
items.reasoning: The authors report null findings at Time 2 and provide supplementary data for exploratory analyses.
